en.html:
Ordinarily, a bleak little park. A few benches, some children's play equipment—bas, that was its entire offering.

Today, though, a different arrangement. Mats, carpets and plastic sheets lay in rows across the ground. Goods of every kind on top, and people selling them.

en.html:
A town of any size would find a suitable square and hold an open market now and then. Kamakura also. Nothing unusual in that.

So many lately, though—that probably belonged to the times.

People who had fled the war were selling the possessions they had brought with them. Sell those, and for the immediate future they could live. Others had escaped with nothing; with their little remaining money, they needed to buy the necessities cheaply.

One side had to sell. The other had to buy. A place for both was needed, and a place was provided. Most of the people here seemed to have come for one reason or the other.

Not everyone. Ordinary citizens were buying and selling also. Muramasa looked about, somewhat bewildered. I urged her to come along and approached one of those stalls.

それなり以上の規模の街なら、適当な広場を使って
折々に開かれる自由市場だ。
　鎌倉でも、別段珍しい催しではない。

　だが最近の頻度の高さには、やはり時勢が絡むので
あろう。

　鎌倉に逃げ込んだ戦災難民が、当座の生活費を得る
ために持ち合わせの品々を売る。
　あるいは身一つで逃げてきた難民が、少ない所持金
で安値の品々を買い求める。

　双方の要求を満たす取引場が求められ、用意される。
　この市も、人出の多くはどちらかを目的とする難民
と<ruby>思<rt>おぼ</rt></ruby>しかった。

　もっとも、どちらにも属さない市民の売り手買い手
とて散見する。
　俺は戸惑い気味に辺りを見回す村正を促して、その
一つに近寄った。

The young woman running the stall was small. Her voice had not accepted that limitation. Welcomed by it, I crouched in front of the mat.

Sculptures, tea bowls, jars, worked precious metals...

Secondhand goods? No, with these one ought to say antiques, or risk causing offense. They did not look like the sort of stock an amateur could handle. Probably a professional antique dealer's stall.

en.html:
Antique Dealer"You are finding fault with my goods? Or you want to beat the price till even its ghost cannot stand up? Either way, valued-customer status is CANCELLED!"
Muramasa"Neither. I have simply given it the correct price."
Antique Dealer"So this is your final statement, madam? Pakka?!"
Muramasa"Hmph."
Antique Dealer"Hah! By the bears of the bloody NORTH POLE, now we have a fight! Come on then, rotating-ears madam!"
Muramasa"THEY DON'T ROTATE!"
Antique Dealer"Then kindly explain! This antique Shigaraki jar, and that ridiculous price of yours—what logic is joining them together?!"
Muramasa"It hardly needs that much explanation."
Antique Dealer"No escaping with clever words!"
Muramasa"...It isn't antique, is it?"
Antique Dealer"—"
Antique Dealer"W-what, wh-what are you saying?! This is definitely from old Edo—"
Muramasa"Mido, when was Edo?"
Kageaki"An era that ended about a hundred years ago."
Muramasa"Your bluff is too big. It isn't even half that old."
Antique Dealer"Arre, muh mein jo aaya—whatever comes to your mouth is not a valuation—"
Muramasa"Twenty-two years and four months."
Antique Dealer"...Huh?"

ja.html:
骨董商「うちの品物にケチつけようってのかなっ？ それとも買い叩こうってのかなっ？ 　どっちにしたってそいつをやっちゃあもう 大事なお客さんじゃあないなあ!!」
村正「どっちでもありません。 　正しい値段をつけてあげただけよ」
骨董商「いいのかいそんなこと言っちまって!?」
村正「ふん」
骨董商「かーっ、北極の熊でおもしれえ！ 　こうなりゃとことん勝負だ、耳がクルクル 回る姉さんよう!!」
村正「回るかっ！」
骨董商「じゃあひとつ教えて頂きましょう！ 　この年代物の信楽壺と今のふざけた値踏み、 どういう理屈で引っ付き合わせるのか！」
村正「理屈ってほどの話でもないけど」
骨董商「逃げ口上は聞けないなあ！」
村正「……年代物じゃないでしょ。これ」
骨董商「――――」
骨董商「ど、どっ、どういうことかなっ!? 　こいつは間違いなく江戸の昔の――」
村正「御堂、江戸っていつ？」
景明「百年ほど前に終わった時代だ」
村正「はったり利かせ過ぎね。 　実際はその半分も無いじゃないの」
骨董商「姉さん、適当吹かしちゃあいけない――」
村正「二二年と四ヶ月」
骨董商「……はっ？」

Muramasa"Twenty-two years and four months since this jar was made. If you know where it came from, calculate it."
Muramasa"It should match exactly."
Antique Dealer"..."
Kageaki"You can tell that precisely?"
Muramasa"What do you think I am?"
Kageaki"I had never imagined you were an expert on antiques."
Muramasa"I'm not, especially. But if it is made from earth or minerals, its age I can tell at a glance."
Antique Dealer"...Aaah, damn it... These Emishi people... How is a person supposed to conduct business...?"
Antique Dealer"Fine... take it at that price..."
